blocking.section: Cutover runbook / Stage 4 shadow traffic; Rollback; Concept mapping / extra_config namespaces (router)
blocking.issue: New regression from the L3-4 and L3-5 fixes. Stage 4 pairing, the per-Route p99 baselines and the Rollback p99 trigger all need one access log record per request, because per-Route Gateway-added time exists only in the access log `gateway_duration` field. The `ruralz_http_gateway_duration_seconds` metric carries only a `listener` label. The runbook assumes `telemetry.accessLog.when` is unset but has no step that makes it so. The importer itself writes `when` from KrakenD `disable_access_log` and `logger_skip_paths`. `when` is a Gateway field in the Bundle, so shadow and serving Nodes share it. Observability also advises busy Nodes to set an errors-only `when`. With `disable_access_log: true`, imported as a `when` that suppresses records, shadow Nodes log nothing and the per-request join has no data. With an errors-only `when`, the Stage 4 baseline and the Stage 5 p99 trigger are computed over error responses only. The runbook also never says that serving Nodes need unfiltered logs at 100% weight, or how large that log volume gets.
blocking.evidence: Line 747: "Shadow Nodes, with `telemetry.accessLog.when` unset, log the same trace ID as `trace_id` beside `route`, `status` and `code`."; line 749: "Record each Route's Gateway-added p99, from the access log `gateway_duration` field ... as its Stage 5 baseline"; line 764: "Each trigger compares one Route over one window, from the load balancer's logs and the serving Nodes' access logs"; line 769: "| Gateway-added p99 of a Route, from `gateway_duration` | More than 50% above its Stage 4 baseline ..."; line 206: "`logger_skip_paths` and `disable_access_log` to `telemetry.accessLog.when`"; Observability, Access logs: "Without it every request is logged, possibly tens of MB per second per Node (hypothesis), so busy Nodes SHOULD set an errors-only `when`"; Observability metrics catalog: "| `ruralz_http_gateway_duration_seconds` | Histogram, fast | seconds | `listener` |".
blocking.fix: Add a Stage 3 step: "Remove any `telemetry.accessLog.when` from the Gateway, including one the importer wrote from `disable_access_log` or `logger_skip_paths`, so shadow and serving Nodes log every request through Stage 5. Size the log pipeline for tens of MB per second per Node (hypothesis). Restore the filter in Stage 6." In Stage 4 rule 4, replace "with `telemetry.accessLog.when` unset" with a reference to that step. Add the item to the Gate summary Stage 3 exit gate. The document is at about 9,488 of 9,500 counted words, so offset the roughly 60 added words by tightening prose that did not resolve an earlier finding, for example the Summary or the Scope paragraph. Do not remove text that fixed L3-1 to L3-14.

non_blocking.section: Migration gaps / Behavior changes to plan for (Header forwarding); Cutover runbook / Stage 1
non_blocking.suggestion: The forwarding item appears on every Route. The Plan cell says "Resolve before Stage 3", but the only mechanism is "None yet". Name the path that is available at M2: an Upstream-scoped `plugin` Policy that calls `request_header_remove` (`request.headers.write`, `onUpstreamRequest`) for parameters KrakenD did not allowlist. Otherwise, the service owner's explicit acceptance. Say whether an accepted item satisfies the Stage 1 exit gate "No unresolved `manual` item".

The research lists `hash` values `plain`, `fnv128`, `sha256` and `sha1`. The fidelity cell covers `plain`, `fnv128`, `sha1` and salted keys, but not unsalted `sha256`, which could map directly to a `sha256:<hex>` digest. State its level. Also say what happens to `propagate_role`.

Stage 5 shifts one load balancer weight for all Routes, so every Route enters at 1%. As written, "enters Stage 5 at the 1% step (target) under closer watch" adds no gate. Either define a per-Route hold at 1% (for example, a longer bake measured on that Route's request count) or say what "closer watch" means.

The baseline for `ruralz_filter_failures_total` mode `open` comes from shadow Nodes on a separate shadow State Store. Their failure rate need not match the production State Store's. Consider an absolute threshold with a (target) tag, or a baseline taken from the first 1% bake.
